title: The Copper Atlas
premise: In 1893, on a storm-battered northern coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Lena Blackwood has spent two years erasing herself from official records to protect a dangerous secret about her late husband's death. When a smuggler named Tomas Ashby washes ashore carrying a letter in her husband's unmistakable handwriting—proof that he lived, and that naval officials falsified the wreck report to cover a cargo scandal—Lena must choose between the invisibility that has kept her safe and the truth that could restore her name but destroy her. Racing three checkpoints manned by men who owe her nothing and fear everything, she and Tomas smuggle the evidence aboard the mail ship before the morning tide. The letter reaches London, her husband's killer is exposed, but Lena learns he is truly gone—and that the life she built in the lighthouse, with Tomas beside her, is the one worth keeping.
about_author: Lior Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the North Atlantic coast. The Copper Atlas is a debut novel inspired by the weathered ledgers, unsent letters, and unexplained gaps she found in the official records.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Opening on the lighthouse during an autumn gale, we learn her routines, her grief, and her careful anonymity—she pays no taxes, answers no censuses. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returns
chapters.summary: Lena finds a half-drowned man on the shingle, clutching an oilskin packet. Tomas Ashby, a smuggler with a broken wrist, wakes in her lamp room. Emotional beat: wary compassion; her instinct is to turn him out by dawn.

chapters.title: Handwriting Like a Hook
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He reveals the packet: a letter in the hand of Edmund Blackwood—Lena's husband, officially drowned two years ago. He doesn't know whose widow shelters him. Emotional beat: the shock of recognition and dread.

chapters.title: Two Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, flashback woven with present. How Edmund 'died,' how she signed the lie, why she vanished from the records. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a hull from deep water.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint: Harrow Gate
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They must pass the customs house at Harrow Gate, where Inspector Vane—a man who once courted Lena—stamps every parcel. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into strategy.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Lena calls in an old favor from the harbormaster's clerk, Mrs. Quill, who owes Edmund a debt no one speaks of. Emotional beat: the fragile arithmetic of loyalty.

chapters.title: Storm Signals
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vane arrives at the lighthouse 'routinely,' but his questions are knives. Lena performs the grieving widow while hiding Tomas in the oil cellar. Emotional beat: terror under a still face.

chapters.title: The Copper Atlas
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Edmund's letter reveals a hidden shipping atlas—copper-engraved charts proving officials ran contraband under naval flags, then burned the crew who knew. Emotional beat: the letter is bigger than one widow's grief.

chapters.title: Ash and Alibi
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Someone has burned the coastal records office. Vane knows the packet exists. Emotional beat: the noose tightening; trust between Lena and Tomas deepens into partnership.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint: Miller's Reach
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The inland toll bridge, guarded by a boy soldier who reminds Tomas of himself. They smuggle the atlas inside a coffin bound for the churchyard. Emotional beat: guilt and dark comedy under pressure.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vane offers her a bargain: the packet for her husband's pension records and legal resurrection. She almost takes it. Emotional beat: the seduction of safety versus the pull of truth.

chapters.title: Mrs. Quill's Confession
chapters.summary: Mrs. Quill's POV. She reveals Edmund didn't die in the wreck—he was put on a prison hulk, and she helped falsify the report under threat. Emotional beat: complicity, shame, and a mother's reason.

chapters.title: The Hulk at Greywater
chapters.summary: Lena and Tomas sail through a rising storm to Greywater to find Edmund alive. They find a grave and a dying witness who gives them the last piece: Vane's signature. Emotional beat: hope's cruel, necessary death.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Quay
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The mail ship Meridian sails on the morning tide; the quay is Vane's territory. They plan to pass the atlas through the one checkpoint Vane cannot search: the mail itself. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vane confronts her at the lamp, offers her Edmund's survival rumor as bait. She lights the lamp for the Meridian and lies to his face. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided in flame.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Mrs. Quill's son, pressed by Vane, betrays their route. Tomas is taken; the atlas is seized—or so Vane believes. Lena has already moved it. Emotional beat: sacrifice as misdirection.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, climax begins. She rows out to the Meridian through the storm's teeth, atlas strapped to her chest, while Vane's men search her empty cottage. Emotional beat: a widow's fury become velocity.

chapters.title: Boarding the Meridian
chapters.summary: Climax. Lena and escaped Tomas fight through the quay crowd; Vane corners them at the gangway. Mrs. Quill publicly names him before the ship's officers. Emotional beat: truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The Meridian sails with the evidence aboard; Vane is taken by his own superiors, who prefer a scapegoat to a scandal. Emotional beat: hollow victory, salt and relief.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letters
chapters.summary: Lena burns Edmund's letter at last, keeping only one line: 'Tell her the light was always hers.' Emotional beat: grief given permission to end.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Spring comes. Lena re-registers the lighthouse in her own name; the records office offers her Edmund's pension and she declines it. Emotional beat: choosing the self she became.

chapters.title: The Light Was Always Hers
chapters.summary: Dual POV, resolution. Lena and Tomas keep the light together through the first calm winter in years. The atlas is published in London; the coast is cleaned of its corrupt masters. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—love chosen freely, duty redefined as the light itself.
